pairs.difference: A: the grey capsule sits at chroma 0.030, below the real 0.082 floor, and takes on the yellow surround (the lens merges the hull into tan). Its underside drains to dead charcoal (shadow kept 0.419, real floor 0.741), and the card is 98% warm with only a thin red band and a blue port as colour. B: the cream envelope has green-tinted shadow edges and a varied pink, orange and teal postcard, though its shadow chroma of 1.605 runs slightly high.
pairs.fix: Paint the hull as cool blue-grey metal with visible cool blue-violet in the shadows. Make the underside a deep rich navy-violet instead of flat charcoal, and keep yellow out of the metal.

pairs.difference: B: the warm mauve-grey rock has chroma 0.041, below the real floor, on a solid orange ground. It has 1.67 hue families (real floor 2.03) and is 99% warm, with pink crystals as the only other colour, so the lens reads as one orange-brown card. A: the yellow and red-orange inflatable on cyan is loud (hue 5.42, slightly over the range), but it keeps a clear warm hero against a cool background, as the real cards do.
pairs.fix: Give the rock a cooler slate-blue and violet shadow side with some dusty teal mineral patches, so it stands apart from the orange background. Lower the background to a slightly deeper, less orange-saturated tone.

pairs.difference: B: warm light tints everything: salmon sky, peach stone with no neutral left, a yellow sun and yellow-green grass (warm 0.657, at the top of the real range). The lens breaks the stone into peach, green and grey patches. A: the sand and castle are a single orange-tan family against cyan sea, with clean green and blue toy accents. All numbers for both cards are in range, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Make the observatory stone a pale neutral grey-beige with cool lilac shadows, not peach. Calm the sky to a softer, less pink tone.

pairs.difference: A: the violet background reaches chroma 0.270, far over the real 0.217 ceiling, and is almost entirely cool (warm 0.002, real floor 0.059). With only 1.61 hue families, the ice-blue comet and its violet ground read as a two-colour card, and the shadow chroma of 1.621 is too high. B: the red scarf is also very pure (0.2165, over the range), but it has a real hero-against-background hue opposition, a gold badge accent and 3.5 hue families.
pairs.fix: Turn the background into a calmer, deeper dusty purple. Add small warm amber glints in the comet's rock and trail, and let the rock's shadows go muted grey-blue instead of saturated blue.

pairs.difference: A: the ball has lilac-tinted whites, a muted purple cap and a red-orange cast shadow on sand, and its shadow chroma of 1.32 is barely over the range. B: the drink is teal and green on blue with a single orange straw. It is 1% warm, well below the real 0.239 floor, but the hue roles are clear and its ice stays pale. The two cards fail in different small ways and neither shows a decisive colour tell.

A: the station, panels, Earth and space are nearly all one blue family (warm 0.039, hue 1.89, both below real). The background chroma of 0.1585 and shadow chroma of 1.611 are both over the ceiling, so the white hull's shadows turn saturated blue, with a thin orange ring as the only warm note. B: the red bike on a pale blue car and yellow dusk scene has a very broad palette (7.15) and greyed shadows (0.47), but it has muted violet-greys that rest the eye.
pairs.fix: Paint the hull in warm off-white with neutral grey shadows, not blue. Use a deeper, quieter navy for space and make the solar panels a muted slate blue.

pairs.difference: A: the yellow canvas bag on purple has a background chroma of 0.223, barely over the ceiling, and a clear complementary hero-against-background role. B: the warm wood, red backdrop and dull green wall have a muted target whose blue-and-white rings give a cool accent, with everything in range. A is only slightly loud, and neither card gives a real colour reason to choose.

A: cyan stripes, a pure purple pot, teal stems, yellow bulbs and orange wood are all near full chroma (subject 0.155), with almost no neutral area to rest the eye, and the hero and background are equally loud. B: the teal book has a wider hue count (6.22, slightly over), but its pale pages, brown wood shadow and cream sticker borders provide resting neutrals.
pairs.fix: Make the pot a dustier plum and soften the stems to a muted natural green. Calm the background to a greyed pale blue so the glowing yellow bulbs are the only loud colour.

pairs.difference: A: the card uses the stock red, cream and sky-blue scheme seen on the generated lighthouses. Red tower and fins sit against a warm-cream body, with bright green grass and sky blue, all at similar loudness, and the white has no cool shadow side. B: the pool bar has a wide hue count (7.05, over the range), but its concrete grey, muted thatch and dark wood shadows carry real local colours.
pairs.fix: Make the rocket body a true white with cool blue-grey shading, not cream. Darken the red to a slightly deeper brick red and soften the grass to a less bright green.

pairs.difference: A: the lime harlequin background reaches chroma 0.2205, over the ceiling, and competes equally with the cobalt globe. With 2.18 hue families, the gold fittings turn yellow-green and merge into the background in the lens, so metal loses its own hue. B: the red, orange, teal and purple balloons are pure, but they spread four separate hues against soft blue sky and off-white cloud (background 0.107), so hero and ground are not equally loud.
pairs.fix: Lower the green background to a softer, deeper muted green. Make the gold stand a warm orange-brown brass with amber shadows so it separates from the green.

pairs.difference: A: the cream parchment is weak at 0.0686, below the real floor, and is washed by orange wood and a violet ground at 0.1872, over the ceiling. Its shadows are orange (shadow 1.597, over the range), and the blue lines are the only colour on the sheet. B: the scroll sits on quiet blues with a red ribbon and gold seal as clear accents (subject 0.084, background 0.146), though its shadow chroma of 1.419 is also a little high.
pairs.fix: Make the paper a paler neutral ivory with grey-violet shading, not orange. Use a calmer, darker purple and a browner, less orange wood.

pairs.difference: B: a silver tube at chroma 0.059 sits on a single hot-pink field. It has 1.56 hue families, 0.878 warm share and shadow chroma of 1.788, all outside real, and the pink floods the shadows and cap in the lens, with one green stripe as a stray accent. A: the blue machine on purple is close in hue and cool (warm 0.026), but the multicoloured cans give it a wider palette and its pale silver trim stays neutral.
pairs.fix: Keep the tube a clean cool silver with blue-grey shadows and no pink reflected in the metal. Calm the background to a dustier rose and let the shelf and table be a neutral soft grey.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away by narrow, over-driven palettes. The background goes above the real chroma ceiling, so hero and ground are equally loud. The whole card collapses into one or two hue families, and shadows are either over-saturated versions of the surface colour or drained to dead grey. In the labelled lessons, neutrals such as metal, white plastic and stone are tinted cream, tan or blue, with no cool, related shadow side and little muted colour to rest the eye; the same habit appears in p01, p09 and p11. Caveat: my picks were meant to rest on colour, but most of them (p01, p02, p04, p06, p09, p10, p11, p12 and possibly p03, p08) are space-themed objects. I noticed this, so subject matter may have raised my confidence beyond what colour alone supports, and p03, p05, p07 and p08 are close to calls with no colour evidence.
